title: Global Payroll SDK Testing Guide (BambooHR)
subtitle: Draft. Last updated 15 Oct 2026: statuses reconciled with Remote's tickets, Slack and sandbox runs up to that date. Rows re-tested after 30 Sep say so.

overview.label: Purpose
overview.value: Test cases for a partner embedding Global Payroll (GP) onboarding and employee bank-detail updates with the Remote Flows SDK and API.

overview.label: Scope
overview.value: Global Payroll only. EOR flows (company creation, credit risk, time off, magic links) are covered in the Company Creation Testing Guide.

overview.label: SDK version
overview.value: @remoteoss/remote-flows 1.59.0 for live tests (7 Oct). Latest release 1.64.0 (14 Oct). Fixes for A2 and E5 first ship in 1.61.0.

overview.label: Token routing
overview.value: Requests to /v1/employee/* use an employee assertion token. All other requests use a company-manager assertion token. Both are minted on a server, not in the browser (see Setup S9).

overview.label: Test country
overview.value: United Kingdom (GBR) GP legal entity. Germany was checked for the personal-details form only. Administrative details also checked on CAN, MEX and SWE (15 Oct).

statusLegend.meaning: Observed live in the sandbox, or read from SDK source where the row says so.
Reproduced defect. Expected Outcome shows the correct behavior; Remote Response shows what happens today.
A fix has been reported. Re-run the test before relying on the result.
Not yet run. Treat Expected Outcome as unconfirmed.
Needs a setting or action on Remote's side.

cases.scenario: Assertion grant enabled for the integration
cases.input: POST /auth/oauth2/token with grant_type urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer
cases.expected: Access token issued
cases.response: If the grant is not enabled: 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Assertion grant is not enabled for this integration"
cases.notes: Controlled by the "Act on behalf of users" setting on the integration (formerly "Create assertion tokens"; API key create_assertion_tokens), per environment. Since 12 Oct it also gates company token creation (POST /v1/companies/{id}/create-token returns 403 without it). Remote must confirm it is on for BambooHR's integration in each environment.
cases.comments: Our test results depend on our own integration's settings. BambooHR's integration is a separate record. Remote said on 12 Oct that BambooHR already has the setting on; confirm per environment.

cases.input: POST /v1/companies?action=get_oauth_access_tokens,send_create_password_email
cases.expected: Company created (201) with data.company.id and data.tokens
cases.response: 422 if "Generate tokens on company creation" or "Allow set password on company creation" is off
cases.notes: Both settings must be enabled on the integration before creating a company.
cases.comments: Full company creation cases are in the EOR guide, Company Creation tab.

cases.input: terms_of_service_accepted_at in the company creation body
cases.expected: Company created (201)
cases.response: Required field. The exact error for a missing or stale value was not recorded.
cases.notes: Must be an ISO 8601 UTC time from the last 15 minutes. Sending it accepts Remote's Terms of Service for the new company.
cases.comments: Use an owner email you control; the owner email cannot be changed later.

cases.input: POST /v1/sandbox/companies/{company_id}/bypass-eligibility-checks
cases.expected: Company passes eligibility checks
cases.response: Success. Status code not recorded.
cases.notes: Sandbox helper endpoints return 404 outside sandbox.

cases.scenario: Create a GP legal entity in sandbox
cases.input: POST /v1/sandbox/companies/{company_id}/legal-entities with {"country_code":"GBR"}
cases.expected: Legal entity created, active, KYB passed
cases.response: Success; entity returned active with KYB passed. Status code not recorded.
cases.notes: Uses the company token returned at company creation.

cases.scenario: Enable Global Payroll on the legal entity
cases.input: POST /v1/sandbox/companies/{company_id}/legal-entities/{legal_entity_id}/activate-global-payroll (no body)
cases.expected: GP product added, global_payroll_enabled set, GP pricing plan created for the entity's country
cases.response: Success. Status code not recorded.

cases.input: GET /v1/companies/{company_id}/legal-entities
cases.expected: Entity shows global_payroll_enabled: true
cases.response: Success. Status code not recorded.

cases.input: Render PayrollAdminOnboardingFlow without legalEntityId
cases.expected: Flow uses the first GP-enabled legal entity
cases.response: Not applicable
cases.notes: Pass legalEntityId explicitly if the company has more than one GP-enabled entity.
cases.comments: Read from SDK source (1.57.0).

cases.input: Run the employee flow in the browser holding only an employee token, with no server in between
cases.expected: Partner routes requests through its own server: /v1/employee/* with the employee token, everything else with a company-manager token
cases.response: 403 on onboarding-steps and the country form schema with an employee token. Writes to /v1/employee/* are blocked by the browser: the x-rf-employment-id header the SDK sends is not in the gateway's CORS allow-list.
cases.notes: The flow's reads need a company-scoped token, which must not be held in the browser. Fixing the CORS header alone would not remove the need for a server.
cases.comments: Direct answer to "can we do this without a backend?": no.

cases.scenario: Create a GP employment through the admin flow
cases.input: PayrollAdminOnboardingFlow on a GP-enabled GBR legal entity; complete basic information
cases.expected: Employment created; flow loads the onboarding steps for it
cases.response: Employment created; onboarding-steps loaded (after A2's extra request)
cases.notes: Requires a GP-enabled legal entity (Setup S5 to S7).
cases.comments: GP employments also created by API on CAN, MEX and SWE (15 Oct).

cases.scenario: Onboarding steps request right after employment creation
cases.input: Create an employment in the admin flow and watch network requests
cases.expected: One GET /v1/employments/{id}/onboarding-steps with the real employment ID
cases.response: First request goes to /v1/employments/%7Bemployment_id%7D/onboarding-steps and returns 404 {"message": "Employment not found"}. The flow then repeats it with the real ID within the same second. Still reproduced on remote-flows 1.59.0 (7 Oct, 2 of 2).
cases.notes: Not blocking; the flow recovers. Partners alerting on 4xx responses will see a 404 on every GP onboarding.
cases.comments: Fix first ships in remote-flows 1.61.0. Not yet re-tested on 1.61.0 or later.

cases.input: Complete every visible field on the Contract details step and save
cases.expected: Entity not on TT2.0: overtime_eligible shown and required. TT2.0 entity: field hidden, not required, defaults to true. Contract details saved in both cases.
cases.response: Verified 7 Oct on a GBR entity not on TT2.0: with employment_id, overtime_eligible is a visible required field and the save returns 200. Before the fix (to 6 Oct): 422 overtime_eligible: can't be blank, with the field hidden.
cases.notes: Fixed by Remote on 7 Oct. Since 9 Oct the contract-details form must be fetched with ?employment_id=; without it the API returns 400 "missing required query parameter: employment_id".
cases.comments: ESP and TT2.0 entities were checked by Remote outside the sandbox, not live here.

cases.input: Same as A3 for DEU, DNK, IRL or SWE
cases.expected: Contract details saved
cases.response: Not run live. Remote confirmed on 9 Oct that DEU, IRL and SWE contract-details schemas never had overtime_eligible, and that DNK has it as an optional field when TT2.0 is off, by design.
cases.notes: The A3 defect does not apply to these countries. A live save is still worth running for each before go-live.
cases.comments: A GP-enabled SWE legal entity and test employee now exist in the test company (15 Oct).

cases.input: GET /v1/countries and read the country's global_payroll_supported and supported_json_schemas (e.g. MLT, Malta)
cases.expected: Partner can tell beforehand that GP onboarding is unavailable for the country
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (partners sandbox): MLT has global_payroll_supported: false and no global_payroll_* forms in supported_json_schemas, and GET /v1/countries/MLT/global_payroll_contract_details returns 422 "Form not available for requested country". Every country with global_payroll_supported: true lists both GP onboarding forms (66 countries); HUN is the one exception in the other direction (see A6).
cases.notes: GET /v1/countries is the simplest way to decide where to offer GP. Reading the form directly also works: a country without it returns 422; a country with it returns 400 "missing required query parameter: employment_id" until it is read for an employee in that country. LVA, the earlier example, has supported GP since October. See Country Coverage.

cases.scenario: Country with only the employer-side form (Hungary)
cases.input: Start a GP onboarding for HUN
cases.expected: Country either publishes both forms or cannot be selected
cases.response: HUN: global_payroll_supported: false; supported_json_schemas lists global_payroll_contract_details and global_payroll_administrative_details but not global_payroll_personal_details, and the personal-details schema returns 422 "Form not available for requested country" (21 Oct, partners sandbox).
cases.notes: The employer can get as far as the invitation, but the employee has no personal-details form to complete. Expected for now: Hungary runs Global Payroll through a local payroll provider, and Remote says the earliest new GP go-live there is March (Remote payroll operations, 14 Oct).
cases.comments: Schema behavior confirmed 7 Oct. Employee-flow behavior on that 422 is unverified. Treat HUN as not available for GP onboarding.

cases.input: Run the admin flow for a GP employment in CAN
cases.expected: Administrative details step loads the administrative-details form
cases.response: Reported on 28 Sep 2026: the step loaded the contract-details form instead. API check 15 Oct: the CAN administrative-details form returns administrative fields (SIN, CPP/QPP, EI exemptions and so on) for a test employee and saves with 200.
cases.notes: SDK step not yet run. A GP-enabled CAN legal entity is now available in the test company, so this is no longer blocked.
cases.comments: If the SDK still shows contract fields on this step, the cause is in the SDK, not the API.

cases.input: Review contract-details labels and options across countries
cases.expected: Labels and options in English, except official local terms, which keep their legal name with an English description alongside in most cases.
cases.response: Not checked for the GP forms. A string audit of contract-details schemas found native-language text next to rough English translations where no direct translation exists.
cases.notes: Not blocking. GP administrative details may also render on the employer side and should be checked.
cases.comments: Confirm which forms the string audit covered before marking Verified.

cases.scenario: Invite before any onboarding form is saved
cases.input: Create a GP employment, then POST /v1/employments/{employment_id}/invite without saving contract or administrative details
cases.expected: Invite refused until contract details are saved
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): 409 "Can't invite employee missing contract details and pricing plan details".
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). Saving contract details is enough to unblock the invite (see A10); the SDK has no separate pricing plan step.

cases.input: Save contract details (PUT /v2/employments/{employment_id}/contract-details), skip administrative details, then invite
cases.expected: Invite accepted once contract details are saved; administrative details are not needed first
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): invite 200. Onboarding steps then show the invite completed and the employee steps not started.
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). Onboarding steps list administrative details as an employee step (employee_provides_administrative_details), so they are not an employer prerequisite for the invite.

cases.scenario: Invite after contract and administrative details
cases.input: Save contract details, then administrative details (PUT /v2/employments/{employment_id}/administrative-details), then invite
cases.expected: Invite accepted: the employer steps are complete
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): contract and administrative details saved (200 each), invite 200. Onboarding steps mark the invite step completed after it.
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks).

cases.input: Complete the employer steps, invite the employee, then call the invite endpoint again
cases.expected: Second invite accepted (200), as a resend
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): both invites return 200 with {"status": "ok"}. The second is not refused.
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks).

cases.scenario: Administrative details saved before contract details
cases.input: Create a GP employment and save administrative details first
cases.expected: Accepted: the employer forms can be saved in either order
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): administrative details saved (200) before contract details. Onboarding steps then show administrative details completed and contract details not started.
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). The invite is still refused until contract details are saved (A9).

cases.scenario: Contract details with a required field missing
cases.input: Save contract details with one required field left out of the request
cases.expected: Accepted: if wage_type is left out, Remote saves it as salary. Send wage_type explicitly for hourly employees.
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): contract details saved (200) without wage_type; the response shows wage_type: "salary". The invite that follows is accepted (200).
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). The check leaves out the first plain required field, which in GBR is wage_type. The form marks it required, but Remote does not refuse the save: it stores salary as the default. An hourly employee sent without wage_type is saved as salaried.

cases.scenario: Contract details with an invalid option value
cases.input: Save contract details with a value that isn't one of the field's allowed options
cases.expected: Request refused with 422, and the error names the field
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): 422 "Unprocessable Entity" with errors keyed by field: wage_type ["Expected data to be \"salary\".", "Expected data to be \"hourly\"."]. Fields that depend on it can be reported too (here annual_gross_salary: "must be empty").
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). The check sets the first required select field (wage_type in GBR) to "not_a_valid_option".

cases.scenario: GP employee on a legal entity without GP
cases.input: POST /v1/employments with type global_payroll_employee and a legal entity that doesn't have Global Payroll switched on
cases.expected: Request refused: only GP-enabled legal entities can engage GP employees
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (NLD legal entity with GP off, partners sandbox): 422 "Global Payroll is not enabled on given legal entity".
cases.notes: Automated flow check: uses a legal entity in the test company with GP switched off, adding an NLD one if there is none (Run flow checks). An earlier message, "Provided legal entity slug is not associated with the Global Payroll product", is no longer returned for this case.

cases.scenario: GP employee with an email address already in use
cases.input: Create a GP employment, then create a second one with the same email address
cases.expected: Accepted (201): an email address is not unique across GP employments. Match employees on employment ID, not email.
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): a second GP employment with the same email on the same legal entity is created (201). Not refused.
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). Remote links profiles that share a login email instead of refusing them. Whether that linking applies to GP employments created through the API has not been confirmed.

cases.scenario: Invite with a start date less than 2 working days away
cases.input: Create a GP employment with provisional_start_date tomorrow, save contract details, then POST /v1/employments/{employment_id}/invite
cases.expected: Invite refused until the start date is at least 2 working days from today
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (GBR, partners sandbox): with the start date tomorrow and contract details saved, the invite returns 409 "The provisional_start_date must be at least 2 working days from today". The same invite is accepted once the start date is later (30 Sep).
cases.notes: Automated flow check: runs in GBR with a fresh test employee each time (Run flow checks). Contract details are saved first so the invite isn't refused for missing them (A9).

cases.scenario: Save personal details (country that requires name)
cases.input: PayrollEmployeeOnboardingFlow, Personal details step, GBR or DEU; fill every visible field and click Save personal details
cases.expected: "Full legal name" input is shown and the step saves
cases.response: Verified 7 Oct on remote-flows 1.59.0: "Full legal name" is shown, PUT /v1/employee/personal-details returns 200 and onboarding completes end to end (GBR). The field also renders on DEU, NLD, AUS and BRA. Before the fix: no name input, and Save did nothing.
cases.notes: Fixed in the SDK. Use remote-flows 1.59.0 or later.
cases.comments: FRA, which does not require name, is unchanged. Endpoint behavior is the same as before: 200 with name, 422 without.

cases.scenario: Save personal details (country that does not require name)
cases.input: Same as E1 for ESP, FRA, IDN, IRL, ITA or USA
cases.expected: Step saves
cases.response: Not run live
cases.notes: These six schemas do not list name as required.

cases.input: Personal details with nationality "GBR"
cases.expected: Accepted, or a clear error naming the expected format
cases.response: "Type mismatch. Expected Array, Null but got String." The field expects an array of display names, e.g. ["United Kingdom (UK)"], not ISO codes.
cases.notes: Elsewhere in these flows countries are ISO alpha-3.

cases.input: Personal details with title "Mr" as displayed in the form
cases.expected: Accepted
cases.response: "is invalid". The API expects lowercase, e.g. "mr".

cases.input: Save personal details, close the flow, reopen it for the same employment
cases.expected: Saved values are shown
cases.response: Every field is blank. The flow loads the form schema but never the saved values, and whatever the employee types overwrites what was saved (remote-flows 1.59.0 and earlier).
cases.notes: High impact: self-onboarding often happens over several sittings.
cases.comments: Fix first ships in remote-flows 1.61.0; not yet re-tested. For USA, Remote added employee GET endpoints for federal and state taxes (9 Oct) so those steps can pre-fill too.

cases.input: Employment whose onboarding-steps response includes a self_onboarding sub-step of type employee_provides_bank_details
cases.expected: Bank details step shown
cases.response: If the onboarding-steps call fails, the bank step is not shown and no error appears
cases.notes: Check onboarding-steps succeeds when a bank step is missing.
cases.comments: Read from SDK source (1.57.0).

cases.input: GET /v1/employee/current with an employee token for an employment that is not yet active
cases.expected: Returns the employee the token belongs to
cases.response: "The employment is expected to be active in order to perform this action"
cases.notes: Cannot be used to debug tokens during self-onboarding, which happens before activation.

cases.input: Employee submits bank details in the flow before activation
cases.expected: Saved via PUT /v1/employee/bank-account
cases.notes: See Bank Details tab for endpoint, token and scope cases.

cases.input: GET /v1/employee/bank-account, employee assertion token
cases.expected: Default bank account returned
cases.notes: Granted scope matched the requested scope.

cases.input: PUT /v1/employee/bank-account, employee assertion token, full bank section with one field changed
cases.expected: Change saved and visible on re-read
cases.response: 200; change confirmed on re-read
cases.notes: Recommended endpoint and token for a partner updating an employee's bank details.

cases.scenario: Company-manager token on the employee endpoint
cases.input: Same PUT as B2 with a company-manager assertion token
cases.expected: Request refused
cases.response: 403 "Forbidden, invalid role for this endpoint"
cases.notes: Refused by role, not by scope.

cases.input: Same PUT as B2, employee token scoped only to bank_account:write
cases.expected: Change saved
cases.notes: all:write is not required. A partner can be granted bank-account access only.

cases.input: Employee token scoped to bank_account:read; GET then PUT
cases.expected: Read allowed, write refused
cases.response: 200 on GET, 403 on PUT

cases.input: Same PUT as B2, employee token scoped to timeoff:read
cases.expected: Request refused
cases.response: 403; the error lists the accepted bank-account scopes

cases.input: PUT with only the changed field
cases.expected: Request rejected with the missing fields named
cases.response: 422 naming every other required field
cases.notes: The whole bank section must be sent on every write. There is no partial-update path.

cases.input: Valid full PUT that leaves out an optional field that was previously set (e.g. IBAN)
cases.expected: Omitted optional field keeps its value, or the request is rejected
cases.response: 200, and the omitted optional field is cleared
cases.notes: A response from GET cannot be sent back unchanged: read and write use different shapes (see B12).
cases.comments: Observed: an IBAN present after UI submission was gone after an API write that left it out.

cases.input: Activate the employment, then repeat B1 to B3
cases.expected: Same results as before activation
cases.response: Employee GET and PUT 200; company-manager PUT 403
cases.notes: Active employees can update their own bank details. Activation does not narrow the permission.
cases.comments: The public reference for PATCH /v1/employments/{id} does not list bank details as editable on an active employment. That list applies to that endpoint only, not to the bank endpoints.

cases.input: Employee adds a second account in the Remote dashboard; partner sends one PUT
cases.expected: Other accounts are not removed
cases.response: Account count stays at two. Only the account flagged default changes; the other is untouched.
cases.notes: A non-default account cannot be read, updated or addressed through this API.
cases.comments: Requires the Remote employee dashboard to add the second account.

cases.scenario: Identify the default account in a GET response
cases.input: GET after several writes on an employee with two accounts
cases.expected: Default account in a fixed position
cases.response: Order is not stable. The default was first before a write and second after it.
cases.notes: Use is_default to find the account a PUT will change; do not rely on index 0.

cases.input: Compare the PUT body with the GET response for the same account
cases.expected: Same shape for read and write
cases.response: PUT takes a flat bank_account_details object (label_name, account_holder, account_number, ownership_type, sort_code for GBR). GET returns an array of objects with is_default, international_details and local_details. label_name is required on write and never returned.
cases.notes: Partners must map between the two shapes.

cases.input: PUT /v2/employments/{id}/bank-account-details with a customer API token, then with a company-manager assertion token
cases.expected: Both tokens accepted
cases.response: 200 for both
cases.notes: Supported. The API reference currently lists only the customer API token and authorization code flow for this endpoint.
cases.comments: Primary recommendation is still the employee endpoint (B2).

cases.input: Employee PUT for an offboarded employment
cases.expected: Request refused
cases.response: Not run
cases.notes: Offboarding cannot be undone, so this needs a second test employment.

cases.input: Not applicable to GP
cases.expected: Not applicable
cases.response: Not applicable
cases.notes: Split payments are not generally supported for Global Payroll. Storing more than one account is supported (B10).
cases.comments: Behavior differs for EOR. Confirm which product a question refers to before answering.

cases.input: GET after submitting a GBR account with no IBAN
cases.expected: No IBAN, or a documented derived value
cases.response: An IBAN came back populated
cases.notes: Unknown whether the sandbox generates it or it is derived. Do not treat a returned IBAN as authoritative yet.

cases.input: POST /auth/oauth2/token, grant_type client_credentials, client ID and secret as Basic auth
cases.expected: Token for the integration itself, valid about one hour
cases.response: Token issued; no refresh token
cases.notes: Can create companies and read reference data. Cannot manage a company's employments.
cases.comments: 401 invalid_client means a wrong ID and secret pair or the wrong environment.

cases.input: JWT signed with the client secret, sub urn:remote-api:company-manager:user:<user_id>, exchanged with the jwt-bearer grant
cases.expected: Company-manager token issued
cases.response: Token issued
cases.notes: sub must be a user ID. An employment ID or slug in its place will not work.
cases.comments: Find user IDs with GET /v1/company-managers?company_id=... using a company-scoped token.

cases.input: Same as T2 with sub urn:remote-api:employee:employment:<employment_id>
cases.expected: Employee token issued
cases.response: Token issued
cases.notes: Used for /v1/employee/* only.

cases.input: Request bank_account:write, bank_account:read or timeoff:read in both the JWT claim and the token request body
cases.expected: Granted scope matches the requested scope
cases.response: Matched in every test

cases.input: Employee assertion for a random employment UUID
cases.expected: Token refused with a description of the problem
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (partners sandbox): 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Subject not found or not managed by this client"
cases.notes: Previously returned with no error_description. Automated check (Run checks): reads only, no token is kept.
cases.comments: Error code and status code are unchanged from before the fix; read error_description.

cases.input: Employee assertion for a real employment in a company this client does not manage
cases.expected: Token refused with a description of the problem
cases.response: 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Subject not found or not managed by this client"
cases.notes: Same message as T5 by design, so the endpoint cannot be used to check whether an employment exists elsewhere.
cases.comments: Fix merged 2 Oct; not yet confirmed deployed to the partners sandbox or re-run.

cases.input: Assertion request on an integration with "Create assertion tokens" off
cases.expected: Token refused with a description of the problem
cases.response: 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Assertion grant is not enabled for this integration"
cases.notes: See Setup S1. The setting is now called "Act on behalf of users".
cases.comments: Fix merged 2 Oct; not yet confirmed deployed to the partners sandbox or re-run.

cases.input: Assertion request signed or sent with a wrong or rotated client secret
cases.expected: Token refused with a description of the problem, which differs depending on where the wrong secret is
cases.response: Verified 21 Oct (partners sandbox), for a company-manager assertion: wrong or rotated secret used to sign and in Basic auth: 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Invalid client credentials". Right secret in Basic auth but the JWT signed with an old one: 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Invalid JWT assertion".
cases.notes: Applies to the assertion, authorization_code and refresh_token grants. Automated check (Run checks): reads only, no token is kept.
cases.comments: "Invalid JWT assertion" usually means the server signing assertions still has an old secret after a rotation.

cases.input: Token request for a disabled integration
cases.expected: Token refused with a description of the problem
cases.response: 400 invalid_grant, error_description "Integration is not enabled"

coverage.title: Country coverage of GP onboarding forms
coverage.intro: Schema check of every country returned by GET /v1/countries in the partners sandbox, Sep 2026. This measures form coverage: a missing form means the SDK cannot onboard there, not that Global Payroll is unavailable. Notes added 15 Oct.

rows.notes: Both are needed to complete an onboarding

rows.measure: Personal-details form does not require name
rows.countries: ESP, FRA, IDN, IRL, ITA, USA
rows.notes: Not affected by GP Employee Onboarding E1
Affected by GP Employee Onboarding E1 until the fix is verified

rows.measure: Contract-details form affected by the hidden required field
rows.notes: See GP Admin Onboarding A3. ESP from the schema only.

rows.countries: GET /v1/countries/{country_code}/global_payroll_personal_details and .../global_payroll_contract_details. A 422 "Form not available for requested country" means the form is not published.
rows.notes: No published list of supported countries exists today.

rows.countries: Estonia and Lithuania have the forms; Latvia does not. Croatia has them; Slovenia does not.
rows.notes: Coverage cannot be inferred by region.
GP forms switched off on purpose: no GP customers there yet (Remote payroll operations, 14 Oct). Not a coverage gap.
Explains the missing personal-details form. See GP Admin Onboarding A6.
Since 9 Oct, Remote reports global_payroll_supported per country, and lists the GP form names in supported_json_schemas. Not yet checked here; could replace the per-form check.
Since 9 Oct, the contract-details form returns 400 without ?employment_id=. Check coverage with the personal-details form, or with an employment.
